title: Higuchi Ichiyō
summary: Born in Tokyo in 1872, Higuchi Ichiyō began earning the family's living after her father died in 1889 and ran a small shop beside the Yoshiwara quarter, which later became the setting of Takekurabe. Nippon.com calls her Japan's first female professional writer. She published Takekurabe and Nigorie in 1895 and died of tuberculosis in November 1896.

uncertainty.note: The National Diet Library gives both dates in full; nippon.com gives birth on May 2, 1872.

where.modern_name: Senzoku, Taitō, Tokyo, Japan (district beside the former Yoshiwara quarter, where her shop stood; she was born in what is now Chiyoda, Tokyo)
where.historical_name: The Ryūsenji area of Shitaya ward, Tokyo, next to the Yoshiwara pleasure quarter

importance.justification: The National Diet Library lists her novels and diaries, and nippon.com describes her as Japan's first female professional writer.

sources.title: Higuchi Ichiyō: A Pioneer of Modern Japanese Literature

reviewer_note: The shop is placed at Ryusenji-machi, Shitaya (NDL) and beside the Yoshiwara in present-day Taitō (nippon.com); the pin is the Senzoku district centroid, not the shop. She lived elsewhere when she wrote her best-known stories; that is not covered by the opened sources.
